resources.string: Detects which app is in the foreground (window switches only, no screen content is read) so WindTone can hide its floating lyrics over apps like the 360 camera view.
Search title / artist / album / file name / pinyin
WindTone doesn\'t scan your whole phone by default.\nChoose how to build your library:
Reads music already in the system media library; with All files access it also picks up .lrc lyrics in the same folders
Only scans the folders you pick. You can choose several and add more later

Features that aren\'t settled yet. They run here for a while, and move to their proper place once they\'re proven stable and harmless to daily use. They are fully implemented — only the entry point is parked here.

This head unit may not have a standalone Accessibility page (common on BYD DiLink). Try any of these paths://n//n1) Settings → System → Accessibility → Downloaded services → WindTone
2) Settings → Apps → Special app access → Accessibility
3) Settings → Accessibility (some models put it at the very bottom of the list, scroll down)
4) BYD DiLink: Vehicle settings → System settings → Accessibility (the app tries this entry first)

If none of them exists, use Usage access instead: it recognises the foreground app with about a 1.5 s delay, which is enough for the per-app hiding list.

Either channel is enough to hide the overlay for listed apps; with neither it is treated as \"do not hide\" and keeps showing. No adb needed: enable the accessibility service in system settings.

Nothing recorded yet. Turn on Record foreground app switches above and drive as usual; when you park, come back to see package names such as 360 camera apps, then tap Add to list to hide the overlay for them.

Playlists, favorites, playback stats and lyrics all stay on this device. Lyrics are read from .lrc / .krc / .yrc files next to the audio first, then from embedded tags.\nThere is exactly one network feature: Check for updates / Download new version contacts the public distribution repository on GitHub (LuckyLearning/Release; it tries the official address first, falls back to third-party mirrors, and can be pinned in Download route). No data is collected or uploaded.
Clears every crash record stored on this device permanently. To report a problem, export the log before clearing.

Removes records of songs whose files are no longer on this device; their favorites, playback stats, lyric offsets and playlist entries go with them. Do not continue if the files are only temporarily unavailable (external storage unmounted, permission revoked). This cannot be undone.

Clears favorites, playback stats, per-song lyric offsets, local tag edits, all playlists, the playback queue and search history. The library and imported folders are kept; playlists cannot be recovered once cleared. This cannot be undone.

Removes every song record and imported folder from the library (including excluded folders). The next launch stops at Choose scan scope and you must pick locations again.

Favorites, playback stats, playlists and per-song lyric offsets are kept — they reconnect automatically when the same files are scanned again.

Audio files on storage are not deleted. This cannot be undone.

Both checking and downloading use this route: Auto connects to GitHub directly first and then tries mirrors; a manual choice uses only that route. Mirrors cache responses and can lag; if one fails, pick another and retry.

Percentage of the screen width (1–100%%). Narrower windows leave more room to move; wider ones wrap long lines later
Continuously adjustable from 12 to 60sp. 16–22sp suits phones; 24–32sp is easier to read from a distance in a car. Applies immediately and is recalculated when the line count is Auto

Brightness kept for context lines: lower values dim them further and make the current line stand out; the default 42%% matches the player (never below 61%% without a backdrop, so it stays legible on light backgrounds)

Nothing configured yet. Floating lyrics hide while a checked app is in front and return when you leave it; if an app is missing, look up its package in About & diagnostics → Debug → Foreground app history

Could not open the system permission page (this ROM has no such entry).\nGo to Settings → Apps → WindTone → Permissions → Display over other apps → Allow.\nSome systems also require Background pop-ups, otherwise the overlay stays hidden after granting.

Permission path: Settings → Apps → Permissions → Display over other apps → Allow.\nSome BYD head units (DiLink) need this app whitelisted or the process force-stopped once; otherwise the screen may stay black or lyrics may not show after granting.

Diagram: width %1$s%% and %2$s; the grey band at the bottom is the head-unit dock (no lyrics within 56dp). See the result on the home screen — full-screen lyrics do not cover this page, so you can adjust while watching.
Tapping Install now opens the system installer; confirm there to finish upgrading. Playlists, favorites and playback stats are kept.
Applies to lyrics that carry both original and translation: it only affects the player and the overlay; lyric files are not modified and translations stay intact when exporting LRC.

How many lines the home-screen floating lyrics show at once (current line centered and highlighted, with context above and below). Auto sizes by the overlay height: a tall window gets more lines, a short one keeps only the current line so nothing is clipped. Selection shows a 6-second preview immediately.

How lyric text is laid out **inside** the overlay window (its position on screen is set by dragging in Adjust floating lyric position and is unrelated). Centering suits lyrics with short lines; left alignment suits long lines — every line starts on the same vertical edge, which reads more easily than the ragged edges of centered text.

Opens the player directly and locks landscape, which suits head units and phones mounted sideways.

Applies immediately: launching turns landscape and expands the player without restarting the app (when off, the current page is not interrupted and the next launch returns to the library).

The library switches to a head-unit layout: horizontal categories on top, larger rows and text, a big playback bar at the bottom, touch targets of at least 76dp, and gestures that are easy to trigger by accident in a car (long-press multi-select, swipe to skip) are disabled.

The player hides the top bar, controls and status row after 5 seconds of inactivity, leaving lyrics, title, progress and time; touching anywhere brings them back. It does not collapse in cover view.

When on, the app starts automatically when the device boots (for car use).

Scheme / presets / band curve / bass / surround / loudness / reverb / fade in-out / volume balance; availability depends on the device audio stack, and some head units only support their built-in effects
